podcast.body: Released in 1969, this was the band's first studio album. Despite containing "Whipping Post," one of their most famous songs (though the live version became more well-known), the album was a commercial flop and "nobody cared" about it upon release. podcast.body: This was the band's first studio album, released in the same year The Band recorded "The Night They Drove Old Dixie Down." Initially, "nobody cared" about the album, with only Lester Bangs from Rolling Stone writing a nice review. Despite containing the studio version of "Whipping Post," it did not achieve fame. The band was not signed by a major label at the time, insisted on remaining in Georgia, and struggled to get radio play. The album's gatefold featured a photo of the band standing naked in a stream, adding to their non-conformist image. "Nobody cared well, Lester Bangs wrote a nice review for Rolling Stone. But really nobody else cared."
